original_card.question: Can a literal QQ16 producer meet the proposed completed-output error budgets with dirty helpers and an affordable physical consumer?
methods: Derive one literal producer's completed-output defects and intermediate dirty-helper bounds, with its physical bill.
Design or audit one consumer, retention or hosting boundary and its complete cost for the pinned producer/decoder.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed premise of the fixed F0/B1 observation obstruction. Show exactly which query is recovered, legal native reads and restoration, and a full favorable budget including cover maps, helpers and endpoints. Local inverse identities alone do not close the global controller. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2965 producer-defect transfer after the local QQ16 decoder contract. Its author-checked output-error estimate does not implement producer interiors, bound dirty helpers, or pay for the consumer; independently check the implication used.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Pin one literal F0/B1 producer and its native-child contracts; derive the actual intermediate magnitude ledger and completed-output defects, including dirty helpers and correlations. Compare with #2965 budgets and price storage, movement, cleanup and F17 consumption. Stop with a precise missing bound if no producer contract supplies it; do not optimize another decoder precision constant in isolation.
original_card.bottleneck_link: The native local words exist; retained query information and its physical access are the missing link to a composed recursive interface.
allowed_variations: One paid query, one changed first pair, or one precisely specified affine helper state.

actual_scope: Price the cut58 source ADDRESS swap on the separable <K,W,T> menu: every P-sandwich inherits one (K,W,T) parity label and the parent polar rank, so this outside adapter does not undercut the per-response tariff.
scope_change_reason: Discussion #1166 comment 19039339 asks whether the q2 event58 suffix can fall to native mass 16. Open PR #4086 already proves a sharp 22f floor for the separable class h*T^e and excludes 16f there. The card remains the joint-query controller, but the donor assignment and that handoff now leave one outside-group adapter. This package prices the source ADDRESS swap named by the cut58 operators, which PR #4086 explicitly places outside its alphabet.
bottleneck_link: The event58 suffix sits on the retained-query side of a recursive interface: prefix 54f plus a 22f separable suffix is 76f against stock 72f. A cheaper outside adapter could be the only remaining way for this fixed endpoint to undercut stock. Showing that the source ADDRESS swap does not lower any inherited response price removes that particular saving without changing kappa.
stop_rule: Stop once every P-sandwich writing is label-unique and rank-preserving and the outside histogram is checked. Do not search the subgroup generated by the menu for a word below 22f, and do not reopen the separable floor.
evidence: PASS_CUT58_ADDRESS_SWAP_MENU. H has order 128 with the PR #4086 rank census; G has order 256; 1024 writings give 1008 monomials, 752 outside G, including 40 extra rank-zero monomials. Every sandwich matches its parent polar rank and the tariff 2(q+(p xor q)+e). PT P, PK P and PW P lie outside G at ranks 2, 2 and 4. The 22f word bound is not extended.

open_questions.question: Can a word whose unaries lie in the 1008-element P-sandwich menu realize the cut58 matrix below native mass 22f?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The per-response tariff did not drop, but PR #4086 counts characters of the separable group only. A same-rank outside sandwich or one of the 40 extra rank-zero monomials might still shorten the word and undercut stock.
open_questions.first_step: Extend one of the three PR #4086 characters to the subgroup generated by the menu, or exhibit one explicit word in the menu whose polar-rank sum is below 22.
open_questions.blocked_by: Direct closure of <K,W,T,P> was still growing past 20000 elements. No cheaper word is supplied here, and the separable character argument is not claimed outside G.
